note: Lesson 7.7 builds an n8n implementation agent; it's shown as steps.

walk.title: Solve it: an AI agent that checks Kora's CRM and proposes changes
walk.sample: Signed design v3 · Telegram approval · sandbox CRM

steps.say: An agent that keeps the CRM matching the signed design. It can read and check freely, but it changes nothing without a person's approval.
show: Read freely · change only by approved plan

steps.say: Store the signed design as data: fields and pipelines in a table, with a version number and a signed date. The agent reads that, never a Word file.
Build the read-only tools first: list the schema, diff it against the design, validate import files, and report data quality. Test each by hand.
The agent runs at temperature zero. Its prompt says the design is the only source of truth, numbers come only from tools, and deletions are never proposed.
show: Telegram (your chat only) or monthly schedule

steps.say: Changes go through a plan with a dry run and a hash. You approve on Telegram, and a separate workflow, not the agent, applies it and logs the change.
Test the guardrails. Requests outside the design are refused, hidden instructions in notes are ignored, edited plans fail the hash, and big plans are split.
show: Not in design → refuse and ask

walk.end: That's the implementation agent: it reads, checks and proposes, and a person decides what changes.
